So:

Substituting j = 2018 − i and using (j+1)/(j!(j+2)!) = 1/(j!²(j+2)):

$$P(2020) = 2020\cdot 2019 \sum_{j=0}^{2018} \frac{(-1)^j \binom{2018}{j}^2}{j+2}$$

## Evaluating the Sum via Integrals

Using 1/(j+2) = ∫₀¹ t^{j+1} dt and the identity $\sum_j \binom{m}{j}^2 z^j = [u^m](1+u)^m(1+zu)^m$:

$$S = \int_0^1 t\,[u^m](1+u)^m(1-tu)^m\,du = [u^m](1+u)^m \int_0^1 t(1-tu)^m\,dt$$

Computing the integral:
$$\int_0^1 t(1-tu)^m\,dt = \frac{1 - (1-u)^{m+1}(1+(m+1)u)}{(m+1)(m+2)u^2}$$

Since [u^{m+2}](1+u)^m = 0 (degree too low), only the second term survives:

$$S = \frac{-1}{(m+1)(m+2)}\left[\underbrace{[u^{m+2}](1-u)(1-u^2)^m}_{A} + (m+1)\underbrace{[u^{m+1}](1-u)(1-u^2)^m}_{B}\right]$$

Therefore: **P(m+2) = −(A + (m+1)B)**

$$P(2020) = -\left(\binom{2018}{1010} + 2019\binom{2018}{1009}\right)$$
